title: The Lekki Headmaster
author: Kabir Alabi Garba
synopsis: Mr. Bepo Adewale — tall, charismatic principal of Stardom Schools, Lekki, Lagos for 24 years — walks to the podium at morning assembly, cannot speak, drops the microphone and weeps. He has agreed under family pressure to relocate to the UK, where his wife Seri works as a nurse. As he prepares to leave, the story looks back over his years at the school and the pressures pushing Nigerian professionals abroad. At Murtala Muhammed International Airport, on the day of his flight, a nightmare about slavery — rooted in what he learned at the Heritage Slavery Museum in Badagry — makes him abandon the journey. He returns to his school and recommits to his students and his country.
setting_place: Stardom Schools, Lekki, Lagos — with scenes in Badagry and at Murtala Muhammed International Airport

chapters.title: Dusk
chapters.summary: Morning assembly at Stardom Schools. Principal Mr. Bepo Adewale, famed for motivational pep talks, breaks down in tears at the podium before students and staff and cannot speak. Vice Principal Mrs. Grace Apeh and others console him; he is escorted to his office, inconsolable.
key_events: Bepo breaks down at morning assembly
Staff and students unsettled by the usually charismatic principal's silence

chapters.title: The Enticement
chapters.summary: Bepo reveals his distress: he has decided to leave Nigeria for the UK to reunite with his wife and children. He reflects on his long tenure at Stardom, his nickname 'The Lekki Headmaster' earned through empathetic and humorous leadership, and his reluctance to abandon his students and the life he has built.
key_events: Bepo decides to relocate to the UK
Origin of the nickname 'The Lekki Headmaster'

chapters.title: Migration Tales
chapters.summary: The wider migration context: the allure of better opportunities abroad against the sacrifices relocation demands. Through friends' and colleagues' anecdotes the chapter weighs the benefits and hardships of developed countries, while Bepo faces trading a stable Nigerian life for an uncertain British one.

chapters.title: A Case of Visa Denied
chapters.summary: Mrs. Ignatius, a Stardom parent, sees her family's relocation plans collapse when a DNA test reveals her husband is not the biological father of one of their children. The subplot exposes the personal and societal tangles of migration.

chapters.title: Snake in the Roof
chapters.summary: During inspection the school MD finds the staff car park full of luxury cars, raising suspicion of financial mismanagement. The cooperative's loan policies come under review to prevent misuse of funds.
key_events: MD discovers luxury cars in the staff park

chapters.title: Comes vs. Come
chapters.summary: Open Day (Parent-Teacher Meeting) at Stardom. A parent's complaint sparks a tense exchange between the principal and English teacher Mr. Fafore. The chapter lays bare teachers' realities: low salaries, housing struggles.
key_events: Mr. Fafore clashes with the principal

chapters.title: Ritualists
chapters.summary: Bepo recalls Beesway Group of Schools, where he once taught. His correction of the school's name ('Group of School') is mocked by director Mr. Egi Meko, who calls the error divinely inspired and misuses words like 'Englisher'. Late one night Bepo witnesses men — the director among them — burying a live cow in ritual; confronting them, he is injured before the director calls them off. Shaken, he weighs reporting it against the cost. He also recalls Fruitful Future, the school he co-founded that failed for lack of infrastructure and government support. A news report implicating one Mr. Ogo in ritual murder closes the chapter.
key_events: Beesway name dispute with Mr. Egi Meko
Mr. Ogo implicated in ritual murder

chapters.title: Missions Unaccomplished
chapters.summary: An unresolved legal dispute between two students' families hangs over Bepo's departure. Stardom elects new prefects democratically: priced intent forms, screening for grades, morals and debt-free status. On Speech Day, Banky (SSS2, Social Prefect aspirant) taunts rival Tosh over his father Chief Didi Ogba's past imprisonment; Tosh storms out. The Ogba family demands apology and legal action, straining the school. Bepo also frets over the Invention Club's Breath Project — phones from recycled materials — fearing his exit may kill it.
key_events: Banky insults Tosh; Ogba family demands redress

chapters.title: Laughing Waterfalls
chapters.summary: Stardom's excursions: Badagry, Whispering Palms, Ikogosi Warm Springs, Erin Ijesha and Owu Waterfalls, the National Museum, the First Storey Building and the Black Heritage Museum. Bepo championed these trips for heritage and holistic education. At the slave-trade sites he draws the parallel driving the novel: historic slavery against modern japa — Nigerians enduring hardship abroad for greener pastures.
key_events: Excursions to Badagry, waterfalls and museums
Slave trade paralleled with modern migration

chapters.title: Passport Pains
chapters.summary: Bepo's expired passport, long ignored, becomes urgent under family pressure. Lagos renewal means bureaucracy, middlemen and bribes, so he goes to Ibadan through an agent, Tai, for extra fees — then stalls again on National Identity Number issues. The chapter is the novel's portrait of public-service dysfunction and what corruption costs ordinary citizens in money and spirit.
key_events: Lagos bureaucracy forces the Ibadan trip

chapters.title: Point of No Return
chapters.summary: Stardom's farewell for Bepo under a banner reading 'For He Gave Stardom His Very Best': a staff-vs-students novelty football match refereed with comic bias by Mr. Ike; an Arts-vs-Sciences debate (arts win on Nollywood and music); and a drama-club cultural display — Bata, Atilogwu and Koroso dances crowned by a canoe dance that moves Bepo to tears over enslaved ancestors. Mrs. Gloss praises his 24 years and presents a $10,000 cheque, the highest ever given a departing staffer; Bepo breaks down in gratitude.

chapters.title: Dawn
chapters.summary: Saturday: flight 10pm, boarding from 5pm, Bepo leaves at 3pm — determined not to repeat missing a flight through carelessness. Landlord Mr. Ogunwale and family pray with him and drive him; he packs iru, egusi, crayfish and dry snail on his wife's advice, and takes Jide's emotional farewell. At the airport VP Mrs. Grace Apeh, accountant Mr. Oyelana and Mr. Audu see him to check-in, then leave ahead of Lagos traffic. Waiting, Bepo sleeps and dreams of counting slaves at Badagry's Point of No Return; an official's tap wakes him to board. Monday: his absence stuns assembly until he walks back in — mission uncompleted abroad, completed at home — to cheers and the school victory song.

characters.name: Mr. Bepo Adewale
characters.description: Tall, charismatic, 24 years at Stardom. Nicknamed 'The Lekki Headmaster' for settling staff quarrels with the wisdom of 'King Oloja' from Village Headmaster while heading the primary section. Dreams of retiring at 55 into farming or transport; co-founded the failed Fruitful Future school. Torn over emigrating to join wife Seri and children Nike and Kike in the UK; chooses to stay.

characters.name: Seri
characters.role: Bepo's wife, nurse in the UK
characters.description: Pushes Bepo to relocate; rumoured to earn over £10,000 monthly. Mother of Nike and Kike.

characters.name: Mrs. Ibidun Gloss
characters.description: Law graduate focused on finances; daughter of the late founder. Suffers a 30-year medical condition. Discovers the 17-car staff park, caps cooperative loans at ₦250,000, and presents Bepo a $10,000 farewell cheque — the highest ever given.

characters.name: Chief David Aje
characters.description: Remembered as a visionary invested in quality education.

characters.name: Mr. Fafore
characters.description: Outspoken; his 'Ade as well as Jide comes' note draws a parent complaint and a wrongful dismissal threat, which Bepo overturns by grammar.

characters.name: Mr. Audu
characters.description: Eccentric, biting humour; lightens the Open Day standoff and sees Bepo off at the airport.

characters.name: Mrs. Grace Apeh
characters.description: Steadfast deputy who manages the assembly breakdown; known for sternness and discipline. Meets Bepo at the airport farewell.

characters.name: Jeremi Amos
characters.description: Efficient, occasionally comic; explains the cooperative loans (₦95M purse, ₦50M+ out) during the car-park inquiry.

characters.name: Mrs. Ignatius
characters.description: Late-night caller; her family's UK relocation collapses when DNA disproves her husband's paternity of Favour.

characters.name: Favour
characters.description: DNA test reveals she is not Mr. Ignatius's biological child, derailing the family's visas.

characters.name: Ikenna Egbu
characters.description: Student speaker at assembly.

characters.name: Jide

characters.name: Mr. Ogunwale
characters.description: Prays with Bepo and drives him to the airport with his family.

characters.name: Banky
characters.description: Taunts rival Tosh over his father's imprisonment on Speech Day, sparking the Ogba feud.

characters.name: Tosh
characters.description: Storms out after Banky's taunt; his family's demand for apology and legal action strains the school.

characters.name: Chief Didi Ogba

characters.name: Chief Mrs. Solape Bayo

characters.name: Mr. Egi Meko

characters.description: Arrogant and corrupt; mocks Bepo's correction of 'Group of School', misuses 'Englisher', and leads the night-time cow-burial ritual Bepo witnesses.

characters.name: Sola
characters.role: Former Home Economics teacher, relocated to the UK
characters.description: Shares the mixed ledger of migration: borrowed for a first apartment, grateful for her asthmatic daughter's emergency care.

characters.name: Hope
characters.description: Migration anecdote: marriage strained after moving, wife withdrawing financial support.

characters.name: Jare
characters.description: Migration anecdote: broke down under the pressure of caring for an elderly couple.

characters.name: Tai
characters.description: Promises faster Ibadan processing for extra charges during Bepo's renewal ordeal.

characters.name: Mr. Ogo
characters.description: Implicated in ritual murder — the twist closing chapter 7, tying back to the Beesway burial.

characters.name: Mr. Ayesoro
characters.description: Deep tribal marks frighten Bibi into nightmares; transferred to another division.

characters.name: Bibi
characters.description: Haunted by nightmares of Mr. Ayesoro.

characters.name: Mrs. Ladele
characters.description: Devoted film fan; mother of Bibi.

characters.name: Mr. Guta
characters.description: Reports Fafore's 'Ade as well as Jide comes' note, triggering the dismissal row.

characters.name: Mrs. Guta

characters.name: Mr. Ike
characters.description: Referees the farewell novelty match with comic bias toward staff.

characters.name: Mr. Justus Anabel
characters.description: Instructed to conclude the assembly after Bepo's breakdown.

characters.name: Mr. Oyelana
characters.description: Meets Bepo at the airport farewell alongside the VP and Audu.

characters.name: Mrs. Titi
characters.description: Leads the weeping principal to his office with the VP.

characters.name: Mrs. Beke Egbin

themes.name: Migration and the lure of abroad
themes.description: The central subject — why Nigerian professionals leave, and the emotional toll of the choice.
evidence: Bepo's decision to rejoin his family (Ch. 2)

themes.name: Patriotism versus economic pressure
themes.description: Bepo's love for country and students set against family pressure for a better life abroad.
evidence: 24 years of service against one flight

themes.name: Systemic dysfunction
themes.description: Corruption, underpayment and poor management in education and government.
evidence: Luxury cars in the staff park (Ch. 5)

themes.name: Emigration as new slavery
themes.description: Bepo links leaving to slave-trade trauma via the Badagry museum.

themes.name: Integrity and community
themes.description: Standing for colleagues and the collective good over personal gain.
evidence: Defending a teacher from unfair dismissal

themes.name: Mental health and leadership pressure
themes.description: The strain a dedicated leader carries in silence until it breaks.

questions.text: Who wrote The Lekki Headmaster?

explanation.key_point: Kabir Alabi Garba — journalist and educator.
explanation.body: The authorship question is free marks for anyone who opened the book. Jalli wrote the *previous* set text (*Life Changer*), which is why she sits in the options.
explanation.trap: 'Khadijat Jalli' is the trap — the author of the book this one replaced.

questions.text: Who is the protagonist of The Lekki Headmaster?

explanation.key_point: Mr. Bepo Adewale, principal of Stardom Schools.
explanation.body: Every major event turns on his decision. The others orbit him — proprietor, teacher, founder.

questions.text: What is the central subject of The Lekki Headmaster?

options.text: The japa syndrome and its effect on education

explanation.key_point: Mass migration (*japa*) and what it does to Nigerian schools.
explanation.body: Every subplot — visas, relocations, the airport — serves this one subject.

questions.text: How does The Lekki Headmaster begin?

options.text: With Bepo breaking down at morning assembly

explanation.key_point: Assembly, podium, microphone dropped, tears — chapter one.
explanation.body: The shock opening inverts everything the school knows about its charismatic head.

questions.text: Why is Bepo under pressure to leave Nigeria?

options.text: His wife Seri, a UK nurse, wants him to join the family

explanation.key_point: Family pressure — Seri in the UK, a better life promised.
explanation.body: The pressure is domestic and loving, which is what makes the choice hard.

questions.text: How did Bepo earn the nickname 'The Lekki Headmaster'?

options.text: For settling staff disputes with the wisdom of 'King Oloja' from Village Headmaster

explanation.key_point: The *Village Headmaster* allusion — wisdom settling quarrels.
explanation.body: Earned heading the primary section, before he ever led the whole school.

questions.text: How does Bepo come to view emigration?

explanation.key_point: Emigration as 'voluntary new slavery' — the novel's thesis line.
explanation.body: Rooted in the Badagry Heritage Slavery Museum. Symbolism JAMB explicitly tests.

questions.text: Where is the climax of Bepo's decision set?

explanation.key_point: The airport, on the day of the flight — nightmare, then refusal.
explanation.body: Setting questions love the airport because it is where the decision becomes physical.

questions.text: How does The Lekki Headmaster end?

options.text: Bepo abandons his flight and recommits to his school

explanation.key_point: He stays. The flight leaves without him.
explanation.body: The ending answers the opening: the man who wept at assembly chooses his students over abroad.

questions.text: Who is Mrs. Ibidun Gloss?

options.text: The Managing Director, a law graduate focused on finances

explanation.key_point: MD, law graduate, founder's daughter — money, not teaching.
explanation.body: Her function in every scene is financial oversight against Bepo's pastoral one.
explanation.trap: 'Vice Principal' is Mrs. Grace Apeh — the two women are routinely confused.

questions.text: Who founded Stardom Schools?

explanation.key_point: The late Chief David Aje — visionary, remembered, dead before the story opens.
explanation.body: Founder questions test whether you know who built what the living merely run.
explanation.trap: 'Mrs. Ibidun Gloss' runs it now as his daughter — running is not founding.

questions.text: Which teacher is known for eccentric humour?

explanation.key_point: Mr. Audu — fine arts, eccentric, biting humour.
explanation.body: One-line character tags are exactly how JAMB tests minor figures.
explanation.trap: 'Mr. Fafore' is the *other* named teacher — outspoken, not eccentric.

questions.text: What literary device is used when emigration is called a 'new slavery'?

explanation.key_point: Symbolism — one thing standing for another.
explanation.body: Emigration *stands for* slavery; the Badagry museum makes the symbol literal.
explanation.trap: 'Hyperbole' tempts because the claim feels exaggerated — but exaggeration is not what makes it work.

questions.text: Where is The Lekki Headmaster mainly set?

explanation.key_point: Stardom Schools, Lekki — post-pandemic Lagos.
explanation.body: Badagry and the airport are scenes; the school is the setting.
explanation.trap: 'London' is where everyone wants to go — nobody gets there.

questions.text: What does the novel's ending say about its central theme?

options.text: That duty to community can outweigh the lure of abroad
That family pressure is always wrong

explanation.key_point: Staying *is* the theme — stated in action, not words.
explanation.body: Theme questions ask what the ending *means*; the flight abandoned means the choice made.
explanation.trap: The novel never says leaving is wrong — only that *Bepo* stays.

questions.text: Why did Bepo clash with Mr. Egi Meko at Beesway Group of Schools?

options.text: Over the grammatical error in 'Group of School'

explanation.key_point: Bepo corrected 'Group of School' — and was mocked for it.
explanation.body: The director called the error divinely inspired and misused 'Englisher', exposing his own ignorance while dismissing expertise.
explanation.trap: 'Unpaid salaries' belongs to Stardom's grievances, not Beesway's.

questions.text: What did Bepo witness at Beesway late at night?

options.text: Men burying a live cow in ritual, the director among them

explanation.key_point: The cow-burial ritual — confronted at personal risk.
explanation.body: Bepo intervened, was injured, and was stopped only by the director's order. The later news of Mr. Ogo's ritual-murder implication closes the loop.

questions.text: What sparked the Banky–Tosh feud on Speech Day?

options.text: Banky taunted Tosh over his father's past imprisonment

explanation.key_point: The taunt about Chief Ogba's imprisonment — said on stage, in front of the school.
explanation.body: The rivalry ran through PTA elections and dance contests, but Speech Day made it public and legal.
explanation.trap: 'Dance competition' is part of their history, not the spark.

questions.text: What is the Breath Project?

explanation.key_point: Recycled-material phones — the invention Bepo fears his exit may kill.
explanation.body: It matters because it is the school's future he might abandon, not just its present.

questions.text: Which sites did Stardom's excursions include?

options.text: Badagry, Whispering Palms, Ikogosi, Erin Ijesha and Owu Waterfalls

explanation.key_point: Heritage sites and waterfalls — education as exposure.
explanation.body: Badagry's slave history beside the waterfalls' natural history: the school teaches the country by walking it.

questions.text: What parallel does Bepo draw at the slave-trade sites?

explanation.key_point: Then: chains. Now: visas. Same desperation, different century.
explanation.body: The novel's thesis in one pairing — and the seed of the airport dream.

questions.text: Why did Bepo process his passport in Ibadan instead of Lagos?

options.text: Lagos offices were chaotic with bureaucracy and middlemen

explanation.key_point: Lagos meant bribes, middlemen and queues — Ibadan via agent Tai promised speed.
explanation.body: Even then NIN issues stalled him. The chapter is the novel's portrait of public-service dysfunction.
explanation.trap: 'Cheaper' inverts it — Ibadan cost extra agent fees on top.

questions.text: Who is Tai, in the passport ordeal?

options.text: The agent who promised faster Ibadan processing for extra charges

explanation.key_point: Tai = the middleman economy in one person.
explanation.body: Promises speed, charges extra, delivers delays — the system personified.

questions.text: What was written on the farewell banner for Bepo?

options.text: 'For He Gave Stardom His Very Best'

explanation.key_point: 'For He Gave Stardom His Very Best' — stretched across the hall.
explanation.body: The banner states the chapter's verdict before a word of the farewell is spoken.

questions.text: What gift did the school present to Bepo at the farewell?

options.text: A $10,000 cheque, the highest ever given

explanation.key_point: $10,000 — unprecedented for a departing staffer.
explanation.body: The amount measures the esteem; 'highest ever' is what makes it memorable, not just the number.

questions.text: What time was Bepo's flight, and when did he leave for the airport?

explanation.key_point: 10pm flight; out the door at 3pm — bitten once by carelessness, twice careful.
explanation.body: He had missed a flight before through oversight; Lagos traffic does the rest of the explaining.

questions.text: What did Bepo dream at the airport, and what did he do after?

options.text: Dreamt of counting slaves at Badagry's Point of No Return; abandoned the flight and returned
Dreamt of his wedding; called his wife
Had no dream; missed the flight asleep

explanation.key_point: The Badagry dream — slavery counted, japa refused.
explanation.body: Woken by the boarding tap, he chooses: back to Stardom, mission uncompleted abroad and completed at home, to cheers and the victory song.
explanation.trap: 'Missed the flight asleep' inverts it — he was woken *to* board, and chose not to.

questions.text: In 'Migration Tales', what happened to Mr. Nku?

options.text: He disappeared after a ₦2M cooperative loan

explanation.key_point: ₦2M taken, man vanished — the cautionary tale of trust abused.
explanation.body: Mr. Nku is why the cooperative later needs caps and oversight; his anecdote earns chapter 5's reforms.

questions.text: What does Sola's UK experience show about migration?

options.text: Its mixed ledger — borrowed for housing, grateful for healthcare

explanation.key_point: Borrowed for the flat; blessed by the daughter's emergency care.
explanation.body: Sola is the chapter's balanced witness — neither japa advert nor horror story.

questions.text: Why did the Ignatius family's relocation collapse?

options.text: A DNA test disproving paternity of Favour

explanation.key_point: DNA: Favour is not Mr. Ignatius's child — visas denied, family in turmoil.
explanation.body: The chapter's engine is mistrust made official by a test result.

questions.text: Why was Bibi reassigned at school?

options.text: Nightmares about Mr. Ayesoro's tribal marks
Her mother's request for a better class

explanation.key_point: Fear, not failure — the marks haunted her sleep.
explanation.body: Ayesoro's transfer follows: the school moves the teacher, not just the child.

questions.text: What did the MD discover in the staff car park?

options.text: About 17 luxury cars suggesting staff living beyond means

explanation.key_point: Seventeen cars — Toyotas, Hyundais, buses — on teachers' salaries.
explanation.body: The arithmetic doesn't work, which is exactly the MD's suspicion and the chapter's engine.

questions.text: What controls did the board impose on cooperative loans?

options.text: ₦250,000 cap plus MD approval for every loan

explanation.key_point: ₦250k cap, MD signs everything, management kept informed.
explanation.body: Against a ₦95M purse with ₦50M+ already out — the 'snake in the roof' gets watched.

questions.text: What grammatical point saves Mr. Fafore?

options.text: 'Ade as well as Jide comes' is correct — the verb agrees with the first subject

explanation.key_point: *As well as* doesn't make the subject plural — *Ade* governs, so *comes*.
explanation.body: Bepo's defence is pure grammar, verified by staff research; the MD's embarrassment is public.

questions.text: Who lightens the Open Day standoff?

explanation.key_point: Audu's humour defuses what the MD's outburst ignited.
explanation.body: His function in the scene is tonal — the scene needs air, he supplies it.

questions.text: What is Seri's occupation, and where does she live?

explanation.key_point: Seri nurses in Britain — the pull behind every relocation scene.
explanation.body: Her profession and place are stated together whenever the pressure is described.

questions.text: How long has Bepo served at Stardom Schools?

explanation.key_point: Twenty-four years — repeated at the farewell and in the banner's praise.
explanation.body: The number measures the devotion the ending rewards.

questions.text: What salary contrast sharpens Bepo's dilemma?

explanation.key_point: ₦400k against £3,600 — the arithmetic of temptation.
explanation.body: Colleagues joke about it; the numbers do the pressuring.

questions.text: What does Bepo dream of doing after retiring at 55?

options.text: Starting a business — farming or transport

explanation.key_point: Farming or transport — enterprise at home, not employment abroad.
explanation.body: The dream matters because it is Nigerian; it answers japa without leaving.

questions.text: How much sits in the cooperative purse, and how much is already loaned out?

explanation.key_point: Ninety-five held, fifty-plus gone — the numbers behind the snake.
explanation.body: Jeremi Amos states them; the board acts on them.

questions.text: Who complained about Fafore's grammar, and what was the sentence?

options.text: The MD; 'Ade as well as Jide comes early' via Mr. Guta

explanation.key_point: Mr. Guta's complaint, the MD's fury, Bepo's vindication — in that order.
explanation.body: The chapter turns on one verb agreeing with one subject.

questions.text: What does 'Englisher' reveal about Mr. Egi Meko?

explanation.key_point: A man who corrects English cannot say 'Englisher'.
explanation.body: The malapropism convicts him in one word — bluster covering ignorance.

questions.text: What price do prefect intent forms carry, and why?

options.text: Priced by prestige, so only the committed apply

explanation.key_point: Higher office, higher price — commitment measured in naira.
explanation.body: Screening adds grades, morals and debt-free status on top.

questions.text: Name two waterfall sites Stardom visited.

options.text: Ikogosi and Erin Ijesha (with Owu among them)

explanation.key_point: Ikogosi Warm Springs, Erin Ijesha, Owu — Nigerian water, Nigerian heritage.
explanation.body: The excursions teach the country by walking it.

questions.text: Who refereed the farewell football match, and how?

options.text: Mr. Ike, with comic bias toward staff

explanation.key_point: Mr. Ike's dubious calls for staff — laughter as farewell gift.
explanation.body: The bias is the joke; everyone, players included, is in on it.

questions.text: Which side won the Arts-vs-Sciences debate, and on what grounds?

options.text: Arts, on Nollywood, music and culture

explanation.key_point: Arts carried it — culture and its economy against utility.
explanation.body: The school that stages Bata and Atilogwu was always going to vote this way.

questions.text: What did Bepo pack on his wife's advice?

options.text: Iru, egusi, crayfish and dry snail

explanation.key_point: Locust beans, melon seeds, crayfish, snail — home, packed.
explanation.body: The list is cultural ballast for the journey; she knows what London lacks.

questions.text: What device is the 'canoe dance' an example of?

options.text: Symbolism — travellers on a river, the journey motif

explanation.key_point: A river journey danced — migration made visible.
explanation.body: It lands hardest because Bepo is about to travel water himself.

questions.text: Why is theBadagry museum central to the novel's meaning?

options.text: It is where Bepo was born
It gives him the 'new slavery' frame for emigration

explanation.key_point: Badagry turns leaving into history repeating.
explanation.body: Point of No Return then; Murtala airport now. The museum is the thesis in a building.

questions.text: What does Mrs. Ladele's subplot (Bibi's nightmares) establish?

options.text: How fear moves through a school — child, parent, teacher reassigned

explanation.key_point: One child's fear reorganises two adults' postings.
explanation.body: Bibi → Ladele → Ayesoro transferred. Fear has administrative consequences.

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.text: Why does Mr Ignatius want to relocate with his family?

options.text: To secure a better future for his children.
To reunite with his extended family abroad.
To enrol his children in Stardom schools abroad.

explanation.key_point: He wants a better future for his children — the reason the DNA result hits so hard (chapter 4).
explanation.body: Answered from our own record of the novel — the chapter summary and character list in this document — rather than from an answer key alone.
explanation.trap: Answering that he wants better pay for himself, which misses what the chapter is about.

questions.subject: use-of-english
questions.text: What disrupted the Ignatius family's relocation plans?

options.text: Mrs Ignatius changed her mind about relocating.
A DNA test revealed Mr Ignatius was not Favour's biological father.

explanation.key_point: A DNA test revealed Mr Ignatius was not Favour's biological father, and the family's plans collapsed (chapter 4).
explanation.body: Answered from our own record of the novel — the chapter summary and character list in this document — rather than from an answer key alone.
